basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 21.' and it opens 'Vers. 21. Hus, ex quo terra Hus dicitur in Job: Buz vero, de quo Buzites, vocatus est'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 21. Hus, ex quo terra Hus dicitur in Job: Buz vero, de quo Buzites, vocatus est Elia quem etiam autumant Hebraei esse Balaam. Gamuel patrem Syrorum. Quod dicit patrem Syrorum non est referendum eis qui hoc nuntiabant, sed potius ei qui longo post tempore scripsit.
